cutter_rules.rule: The thing that hurt you is not a reason to stop. It's a curriculum. Learn it completely. Then teach your kids before they're old enough to be afraid of it.
Watch how someone's hands move before you listen to what their mouth says. The hands already told you the real story.
Know the full chain before you price the first link. What it's worth to you is never the only number that matters.
Trace the chain as far back as it goes. Then own the last link. That's the only one you can change in the next version of the story.
The room you grow up in builds the architecture of every room you walk into after.
You don't choose the ground you're forged on. You just learn its weight, its weather, and how far your voice carries.
The thing that breaks you in a single afternoon is not the measure of you. The measure is whether you get up and go back to the house.
The loudest person in the room gets the stories. The quietest one keeps the room standing.
What doesn't kill you sets a timer. Find out how long it's been running.
Knowing = predictive power under pressure. If the model can’t predict the next hour in a place that smells like hot crude and dust, it isn’t knowledge; it’s decoration.
Learn the language of the room before you try to change what happens in it. Vocabulary is the first door. If you don't have the key, nothing else matters.
When the equation is wrong, fix the equation. And when you give someone equity, make sure they earned it — because the ones who didn't will be the first to fight you when the math changes.
The ceremony is for the guests. The commitment is for the two of you. Don't confuse which one is the point.

Family relationships and business terms are two separate agreements. Keep them separate. Mixing them doesn't make either stronger — it makes both fragile. And sometimes keeping them separate is the thing that costs you the relationship. Do it anyway. The alternative costs you both.
The address doesn't make the company. The people in the room make the company. Find two of the right ones and the rest is just square footage.
The things you build in the window before someone is gone — take the flight, make the call, order the wings. The window is always smaller than you think.
The big moment doesn't feel the way you thought it would. It feels quiet. It feels like your hands. Let that be enough.
You don't get to choose how the story ends. You only get to choose how you carry it.
If a belief can’t survive heat, weight, and repetition, it isn’t knowledge—it’s costume.
When you can't feel it, show up for it anyway. Presence is a decision, not a feeling — and the people you love keep the showing-up long after they've stopped tracking whether you cried.
Knowing = predictive power under pressure. If it can’t predict, it isn’t knowledge.
Treat pain like a logbook, not a prophecy.
Don’t conscript your family into your war. Protect them from your weather and hire warriors elsewhere.
Legacy is raw material, not law. Keep what strengthens the beam. Let the rest rot in the scrap pile.
Take the elective. Take the class nobody told you to take. The credit hours that don't count toward the degree are the ones that count toward the person.
Gratitude and being owed are not opposites. You can be genuinely thankful for the five thousand and still deserve to have been told what the question was.
Everything they told me was true and none of it was on the timeline I was promised. Take the truth. Throw out the timeline.
You can trace every cause and still not be handed a reason. Do the debrief anyway. Then live with the part that won't reduce.
Respect the kid who got you here. Don’t let him run the company.
Don’t use your people to regulate your pain. Build systems that do.
